<p>Model-Saver: Write the SWA pattern, 15 more architectures roundtrip (<a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="5490616581" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/29042" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29042/hovercard" href="https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29042">#29042</a>)</p>
<ul>
<li>llama: read the SWA pattern as a period or a per-layer array</li>
</ul>
<p>Add llama_model_base::load_swa_pattern(), which reads<br>
sliding_window_pattern either as one flag per layer or as a period<br>
expanded by set_swa_pattern(), and use it in every loader that reads<br>
the key as a period.</p>
<p>These loaders silently ignored an array and applied their default<br>
period, although the converters of olmo2, gemma3n and exaone4 write<br>
arrays. The published GGUFs match the defaults, so their outputs do<br>
not change. The loaders that already accepted both forms lose their<br>
duplicated scalar-then-array block, and use their declared default<br>
period when the key is absent.</p>
<ul>
<li>model-saver: write the SWA pattern and the MLA SWA geometry</li>
</ul>
<p>Write sliding_window_pattern as one flag per layer, nextn layers<br>
included, for every model using SWA. The array is never collapsed to<br>
a scalar, since the loaders read a scalar as a period.</p>
<p>Also write the MLA key/value lengths and KV LoRA rank of the SWA<br>
layers, required by dots3note.</p>
<p>This enables the saver for plamo3, gemma3, cohere2, cohere2moe,<br>
olmo2, exaone-moe, afmoe, mimo2, spark2_5, muse-glimmer, mellum,<br>
laguna, granite_swa, dots3note and maple, all passing the bit-exact<br>
roundtrip of test-llama-archs.</p>
</details>

    <title>b11029</title>
    <content type="html"><details open="">
<p>vulkan: raise the hoisted row-id limit for mul_mat_id from 256 to 1024 experts (<a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="5366076039" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/28501" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28501/hovercard" href="https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/28501">#28501</a>)</p>
<ul>
<li>vulkan: raise the hoisted row-id limit for mul_mat_id to 512 experts</li>
</ul>
<p>The expert-count shader (count_experts.comp) sizes its shared arrays<br>
with BLOCK_SIZE, which is 256. Because of that, row-id hoisting is<br>
switched off for any model with more than 256 experts, and every<br>
mul_mat_id workgroup has to rescan the whole ids tensor on its own.<br>
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next has 512 experts and was quietly running on that<br>
slow path.</p>
<p>This change sizes the arrays with a separate MAX_EXPERTS constant (512),<br>
clears them in a loop instead of one entry per thread, and raises the<br>
matching limit on the host side.</p>
<p>On Strix Halo at batch 2048 the expert matmuls drop from 12.5 to 9.5 ms<br>
(iq3_s) and from 14.0 to 7.5 ms (iq4_nl) per op, and prompt processing<br>
gets about 19 % faster at 8k tokens. test-backend-ops MUL_MAT_ID passes<br>
(891/891) with new 512-expert test cases.</p>
<p>Assisted-by: Claude Fable 5.1</p>
<ul>
<li>vulkan: raise the hoisted row-id limit for mul_mat_id to 1024 experts</li>
</ul>
<p>Follow-up to review feedback: 1024 matches LLAMA_MAX_EXPERTS instead of<br>
stopping at 512. The three shared arrays in count_experts.comp grow to<br>
3 * 1024 * 4 = 12 KiB, which fits the 16 KiB that Vulkan guarantees for<br>
maxComputeSharedMemorySize.</p>
<p>Adds mul_mat_id test cases at 1024 experts alongside the existing 512<br>
ones. test-backend-ops MUL_MAT_ID passes on Vulkan (RADV, Strix Halo,<br>
Radeon 8060S): 889/889.</p>
